title: WORD SPRING
territory: Voice wells up into short, stable rows of written language.
oneSentenceMeaning: A rising body of voice finds its footing in three clear lines of text.
appIdentity: Mluva is the small daily pleasure of speaking a thought and finding something useful waiting in your editor. Its Czech name means speech, and its home is Omarchy: a working desktop where tools should feel immediate, legible and quietly personal. Dictation begins with your voice; rewriting can give the resulting words another shape. The original recognition remains available beside saved working versions and completed results, so improvement does not erase the source. Local and cloud providers are choices within that experience, rather than claims embedded in the identity. Editable Markdown, exact text and a dependable place to return to a thought give the delight practical substance. Word Spring expresses that movement from available expression to settled language. It supports “Most delightful dictation for Omarchy” and “A little more delight every day” through a small, satisfying act of formation, without making promises about recognition accuracy or response time.
markIdentity: Word Spring gives speech a visible consequence: three short horizontal rows supported by one rising mass. The eye should first register a compact, confident symbol, then discover that its soft lower origin becomes the order of written language. The source is broad and integral. It does not appear as a droplet, a separate sound wave or a decorative flourish. The rows remain level while the left side climbs, making a useful tension between human expression and a stable result. A single solid silhouette carries the idea across themes, launcher sizes and the closing film frame. Three rows are enough to suggest a passage of writing without drawing a document. Their unequal ends keep the passage alive; their equal weight keeps it calm. The desired character is generous, articulate and lightly surprising. The mark belongs to an everyday writing companion, with enough discipline for a technical desktop and enough warmth to make returning to it pleasant.
logoDescription:
The final mark is one compact filled shape, approximately as tall as it is wide. A broad, softly curved heel begins at the lower left and rises diagonally toward the upper centre. Along its right side it resolves into three thick, perfectly horizontal ledges. These ledges are the written rows. Two deep channels, open to the right, separate them. There is no enclosing perimeter, border, speech tail, detached droplet or containing tile. The distinction between the curved source and the level output must be visible in the silhouette itself.

Use a nominal 24-unit study grid with visible bounds near x=3–21 and y=3–21. Place the three row bands approximately at y=3–7, y=10–14 and y=17–21. The upper row reaches x=21, the middle x=20 and the lower x=17. Their left roots move progressively left as they descend, joining the continuous diagonal source. The two channels retain at least three units of open height. Treat these coordinates as construction targets for optical refinement, rather than claiming they are verified production geometry.

The left boundary is one restrained convex climb, not a sequence of scallops. It has enough thickness to carry the rows through reduction without thin necks. Its lowest turn is rounded and gently compressed against the baseline; it never sharpens into a leaf point. On the right, use nearly square row ends with only a small corner easing. Full capsule ends would turn the writing into a generic interface menu. Keep the horizontal faces flat and use a slight optical weight correction where the source joins each ledge so the junctions do not become dark knots.

The uneven right edge and oblique source deliberately disturb a literal capital E. The mark should feel like language coming into existence, not an initial for another name. Its meaning must remain plausible without animation, colour or the title Word Spring. At small size, the priority is the memorable rising silhouette and three open divisions; the more specific speech-to-writing association can become clearer through repeated use beside Mluva. This is a study direction. If a drawn candidate reads first as a feather, stairway or letter E, revise the source proportions before accepting it.
wordmarkDescription:
Write exactly Mluva, with an uppercase M and lowercase luva. Start from JetBrains Mono Medium, preserving the familiar technical clarity that already connects Mluva’s application and film. Turn the five glyphs into editable filled shapes and sculpt their proportions; a default font sample with ordinary tracking is not the proposed result. The wordmark should be calm at first glance and reveal a small coordinated gesture on closer inspection.

Keep the M upright, with straight outer stems and a clear internal valley. Narrow its overall width modestly only if the first pair otherwise looks detached. Retain the l’s short identifying head and a concise rightward foot, while reducing its advance substantially from the monospace cell. The l must remain unmistakably lowercase and must not become an anonymous vertical bar. Let its bottom turn begin softly and finish on a short level terminal: this is the most direct typographic echo of the spring becoming a row.

Give the u a generous interior and a slightly flattened base with a smooth, restrained rising turn into its right stem. Preserve the v’s clear diagonal construction, opening its upper space and relieving the darkest point at the lower vertex by a tiny optical adjustment. Retain a recognisable double-storey a with an open, readable upper space and a comfortably sized lower counter. Its terminal ends level, providing a composed finish. Keep these gestures subtle; none of the letters becomes a pictogram or borrows the entire symbol’s three-row construction.

Set spacing by the visible white shapes between letters. Tighten M–l enough to unite the opening, then tune l–u, u–v and v–a individually so the diagonal pairs do not seem to float apart. Equal character advances are unnecessary. All five letters share one baseline and one ink weight, with minimal overshoot for curved forms. Use solid monochrome ink on actual transparency. The resulting wordmark should preserve immediate reading as Mluva at ordinary interface sizes, while a larger title reveals the softened rise and steady landing that connect it to Word Spring.

selfCritique.issue: The first arrangement was a rounded E with three equal rightward arms.
selfCritique.whyItMatters: The viewer could reasonably infer an unrelated initial, a menu command or an editor category. Explaining a spring afterward would not rescue an indistinct symbol.
selfCritique.change: Replace the straight left spine with a substantial oblique source, shorten the lower endpoint and give the three row roots different horizontal positions.
selfCritique.residualRisk: An E association can still dominate if the source becomes too upright. Judge the unlabelled silhouette before showing the concept title.

selfCritique.issue: A soft lower bulb made the origin read as liquid, while a thin tapered origin looked like a feather.
selfCritique.whyItMatters: Either reading would make this a decorative derivative of the film’s water material and weaken the connection to useful language.
selfCritique.change: Use a broad compressed heel with a blunt baseline contact, one controlled outer curve and no detached bead, pointed tip or central vein.
selfCritique.residualRisk: The diagonal profile still has an organic association. Keep the level rows visibly dominant and avoid stretching the mark into a tall leaf.

selfCritique.issue: Three rows can collapse into a hamburger menu or an ascending chart.
selfCritique.whyItMatters: A utility icon would be easy to use but difficult to recognise as Mluva. A growth chart introduces a performance story absent from the product.
selfCritique.change: Maintain one connected source, equal row thickness and horizontal alignment within each row. Use an irregular endpoint sequence rather than a regular staircase of increasing bar lengths.
selfCritique.residualRisk: The row ends at 21, 20 and 17 remain an ordered visual progression. Optical drawing should preserve the uneven rhythm rather than regularise it.

selfCritique.issue: The written explanation is more expressive than an untested 24-pixel drawing.
selfCritique.whyItMatters: Concept prose can conceal a mark that needs its caption. No raster comparison has been performed within this text-only task.
selfCritique.change: Specify generous three-unit channels and four-unit row bands, make the required unlabelled checks explicit and describe the coordinates as study targets.
selfCritique.residualRisk: Readability and distinctiveness remain unverified until the parent study renders and inspects the mark at actual size.

selfCritique.issue: Applying the same spring gesture to every letter made the name look mannered.
selfCritique.whyItMatters: Mluva should read immediately; excessive hooks, lifted baselines or forced ligatures would make it look like a font experiment.
selfCritique.change: Concentrate the distinctive turn in the narrowed l, echo it lightly in u and the a terminal, and retain the M and v as structural anchors.
selfCritique.residualRisk: The wordmark may still look too close to standard JetBrains Mono unless the l advance and pair spacing receive real optical work.

selfCritique.issue: A source turning entirely into polished rows could imply that Mluva replaces or perfects the original.
selfCritique.whyItMatters: The product preserves raw recognition separately, and a rewrite still needs review.
selfCritique.change: Keep the source visibly present in the final mark and hold completed rows steady in the proposed motion. Describe formation and usefulness without accuracy or latency claims.
selfCritique.residualRisk: An abstract mark cannot communicate the full source contract; product copy and demonstrations must continue to explain it.

revision: The initial direction used a rounded vertical source with three similarly long arms. Its apparent simplicity concealed three weak readings: a lowercase utility glyph, a wet brushstroke and a menu icon. The revised final is a single dense rising paragraph. Its source crosses the height diagonally, beginning in a compressed, broad lower heel. Three flat, four-unit bands extend from that source, divided by generous open channels. Their right ends are unequal without becoming a regular bar chart. The lower turn carries the warmth; the straight written rows carry the precision. No ornamental droplet, source dot, accent slash or second colour is retained. The wordmark revision removes repeated decorative hooks and a proposed u–v connection, leaving five independent, immediately recognisable letters. JetBrains Mono remains legible in the skeleton, while the narrowed l, its soft-to-level foot, measured u base and individually corrected spacing establish a specific relationship to the mark. This is the final concept specification for comparison, not an approved production asset. The outstanding decision is visual: an unlabelled 24-pixel rendering must read as a distinctive rising form with clear rows, and must not be accepted merely because the accompanying story explains it.
logoPrompt: Create one logo symbol only for the Mluva Word Spring study. The image must have actual transparent alpha around the artwork. Draw one compact, fully solid monochrome near-black ink silhouette, approximately square. A broad, gently curved source rises diagonally from a compressed rounded heel at the lower left toward the upper centre. Its right side becomes exactly three thick horizontal text rows, connected into the same filled mass. Two generous horizontal negative channels open all the way to the right. On an imagined 24-unit grid, visible bounds are approximately x=3–21, y=3–21; row bands occupy y=3–7, 10–14 and 17–21; upper, middle and lower right ends reach approximately x=21, 20 and 17. Left roots step inward along the broad rising source. Keep the channels visibly open, the row faces flat and the right ends nearly square with only tiny corner easing. Use one clean convex left boundary, no vertical E-like spine, no thin necks and no pointed lower tip. The result should suggest voice welling up into short stable written rows, with a strong immediately memorable 24-pixel silhouette. It should feel calm, useful and lightly delightful. No lettering, wordmark, concept label, captions, mockups, app tile, container, white background, checkerboard texture, gradients, shadows, glow, outlines, strokes, water blob, bubble, microphone, page corner, feather vein or copied brand geometry. Centre the single symbol with generous transparent space. Render only the final revised symbol.
wordmarkPrompt: Create the wordmark only, reading exactly Mluva, uppercase M followed by lowercase luva. Use actual transparent alpha; all letter shapes are solid monochrome near-black ink. Start with the recognisable skeleton of JetBrains Mono Medium and visibly refine it into custom lettering. Keep an upright M with straight outer stems and a clear diagonal valley. Narrow the lowercase l and its character advance, retaining a short identifying head and a softly turning foot that finishes in a concise level terminal. Give the u a generous counter and a subtly flattened, smoothly rising lower turn. Preserve the clear diagonals of v with only minute optical relief at its bottom vertex. Keep a readable double-storey a with generous internal space and a level final terminal. Tune the white space of M–l, l–u, u–v and v–a individually; do not leave equal monospace advances or mechanically uniform tracking. Preserve a common baseline, coherent weight and immediate legibility. The character should be calm, precise, welcoming and quietly distinctive, with the subtle sensation of expression settling into written language. Do not add a symbol, spring illustration, row motif inside a letter, ligature, tagline, label, explanatory text, mockup, container, tile, white background or checkerboard texture. No outlines, strokes, gradients, shadows, glow, three-dimensional effects or additional colours. Show one refined horizontal Mluva wordmark with generous transparent margins.
smallSizeRisks: At 24 px, the two open channels may close through antialiasing. Target approximately 3 px of clear height and inspect the actual raster; do not treat the coordinate plan as proof.
The diagonal source can become either a thin feather stem or an upright E spine. Keep a broad connection and enough lateral travel for the rising gesture to survive.
Rounded row ends may erase the distinction from a menu icon. Corner easing should remain much smaller than half the row thickness.
The compressed heel may become an isolated dark lump at 16 px. A later small-size master may need local weight reduction without detaching the source.
The symbol’s semantic reading is less certain than its structural reading. Test it without the wordmark and title; a persistent feather or E reading is a reason to redraw.
In the wordmark, narrowing l too far can turn Mluva into an ambiguous run of stems. Preserve the head and foot and inspect the M–l and l–u gaps at the intended use size.
opticalRules: Use filled geometry only. The logo is one connected ink mass with two open channels, not an outline expanded from a thin path.
Construct around a 24-unit nominal grid, with approximately 18 units of visible width and height, four-unit row bands and at least three-unit channel openings.
Keep exactly three rows. Extra rows reduce the source to a comb; two rows weaken the written-passage reading.
Keep all written row faces horizontal. The source supplies the upward motion; the text supplies stability.
Offset right endpoints unevenly: the upper and middle are close, the lower clearly shorter. Do not regularise them into an ascending chart.
Use a broad oblique source with a blunt lower heel, no vertical spine, no fine stem and no pointed leaf tip.
Ease corners locally rather than making every end a capsule. Reduce excess ink where the source meets the rows.
Evaluate solid ink and its light reversal as the same silhouette. Theme adaptation changes the single ink colour, never the geometry or interior opacity.
Optically centre the ink mass within its clear space; geometric centring may place the heavier lower-left source too low.
Keep the wordmark’s five glyphs separate, tune pair spacing by eye and preserve unmistakable Mluva spelling. Retain JetBrains Mono provenance if developed into actual artwork.
motionRelationship: For a future brand reveal, the broad source makes one quiet upward movement and the three row ends extend into their final positions. Settle each row once and leave it steady while the next forms, echoing the product’s treatment of stable text. Keep the source present throughout; it should never dissolve into supposedly perfected output. A short authored reveal of roughly 600–900 ms is a design proposal, not a product latency claim. No elastic overshoot, liquid splashing, waveform oscillation or perpetual logo breathing is needed. The existing film’s water footage may remain an independent surrounding material; the symbol stays solid and legible over it. The existing 3.4-second breathing cadence belongs to recording feedback and does not need to reshape this mark. Reduced motion shows the complete final symbol immediately. Any later animation study should end on exactly the same geometry as the static mark and should preserve that final hold beside the Mluva wordmark.
